summary.headline: Suzlon Q2 FY27 revenue rose 27% QoQ to INR4,869 crores, but WTG contribution margin fell to 21.2% and FY27 EBITDA margin guidance was cut to about 15%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 delivered sequential growth: revenue INR4,869 crores (up 27% QoQ), EBITDA INR720 crores (up 21% QoQ) and PAT INR394 crores (up 29% QoQ). Year-on-year, EBITDA margin fell to 14.8% from 18.8%, driven by customer/scope mix, commodity and FX volatility linked to the West Asia crisis, and non-recurring Suzlon 2.0 opex. Management reset the FY27 EBITDA margin view to about 15.1% plus up to 1% from H2 operating leverage, down from the earlier roughly 17% expectation. Commissioning rose 69% QoQ to 454 MW, and net worth crossed INR10,000 crores with net cash of about INR2,048-2,300 crores (figures quoted differently in the call).

segments.name: Wind turbine generators (WTG)
segments.commentary: Contribution margin 21.2% vs 26.9% a year ago; management guides 22-23% for FY27, subject to commodity/FX normalisation. Q2 deliveries 710 MW, up 40% QoQ, a record second quarter for India deliveries.

segments.name: RE AMS (service)
segments.commentary: Installed base above 16.5 GW with EBITDA margins maintained above 40%; higher-margin service mix is shrinking as WTG revenue grows (about 50 bps impact).

segments.name: Foundry and forging
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR167 crores and EBITDA INR50 crores, with growth from domestic demand and exports.

segments.name: Renom (acquired ISP business)
segments.commentary: About 178 MW added in H1 FY27 and close to 200 MW of orders won in the last quarter; management frames it as a long-term scale-up opportunity. A shareholder questioned the roughly INR700-800 crore acquisition cost against small annual profit.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin: about 15.1% for H1 plus 1% H2 leverage (H2 expected at 1.5x-1.65x H1 volumes); management said 17% possible if commodity/FX eases.
WTG contribution margin expected at 22-23% for FY27, subject to West Asia-linked commodity and FX normalisation.
Non-recurring Suzlon 2.0 opex of about INR50 crores in Q2 (about 1% margin impact) expected to phase down.
Suzlon 2.0 targets: India market share 40% by FY31 (currently about 28-29% in order terms), order book from 6 GW to 15 GW by FY31, 25% CAGR, exports 3 GW order book and 1 GW sales by FY31.
Deferred tax asset recognition to be assessed annually, next in March 2027.
capex_capacity: Installed manufacturing capacity 4.5 GW, fully operational, using 3.3 MW turbine; blade capacity to be expanded via new blade plants for higher-MW turbines.
Commissioning 454 MW in Q2 (up from 269 MW) and 723 MW in H1 FY27 (up 168% YoY); about 1.25 GW erected and awaiting commissioning; about 3.9 GW pending installation, of which about 1.3 GW erected.

Capital allocated to DevCo about INR500 crores in total; net deployed about INR125-130 crores after some assets were sold. No capex yet on solar/BESS, which is planned as asset-light, with capex starting after next couple of quarters.
Three AI-enabled smart blade factories being set up; S175 5.X MW prototype commissioned, first order of 21 turbines (105 MW).
demand_pricing: Order book 6 GW, covering about 18 months; 1.5 GW of new orders in H1 FY27; about 900 MW booked via DevCo in H1; about 78% of the order book is C&I and PSU/utility.
Industry: about 8-9 GW of wind RTC/FDRE/wind-dominated tenders awarded in H1 FY27; India at 59 GW installed wind capacity, with 15 GW annual installations targeted by FY31.
Market share: about 28-29% in order terms in H1; about 23% in deliveries in H1.
Pricing: management said there were no price cuts; ASP dip attributed to business mix (EPC vs supply-only, project stage).
Competition: Adani, JSW and others expanding; management says large part of their output is captive. Existing customers such as NTPC, Aditya Birla Renewables and Purvah are said to remain customers.

Exports: INR12,000 crore wind equipment exports from India in FY26 (industry figure); Blue Sky 5 MW and 6.3 MW certification in progress; 2.1 MW small turbine interest; first repowering order in India with Tata; export orders expected to be reported next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the WTG contribution margin fall to 21.2%, and when will fixed-cost pressure and operating leverage show?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin decline to customer/scope mix (150-180 bps), segment mix (about 50 bps), non-recurring Suzlon 2.0 opex (about 100 bps) and commodity plus FX (about 50 bps). Operating leverage from H2 volumes is expected to add about 100 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Is the working capital stretch linked to DevCo, and why are receivable days up QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Jain said DevCo is not the driver. Inventory is being built for H2, and receivables are higher due to commissioning-linked holds (5-10% of revenue per customer), which should convert to cash as commissioning rises.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the finance cost running above the INR300 crore guidance, with H1 above INR250 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 is not a simple multiple to project because volumes and revenue are up. It said like-for-like interest costs are falling, and levers are being used to manage working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Why are installations lagging deliveries and what is stopping faster ramp-up with 4.5 GW capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajay Kapur said capacity is not the constraint; project pull is. He expects about 18 months for sharper commissioning after regional chief project officers were appointed. He expects 25% CAGR and 10 GW annual sales by FY31.

qa_highlights.question: What is the update on localisation/ALMM and its effect on competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ALMM covers six components (nacelle, blade, tower, generator, gearbox, special bearings), with grandfathering extended to 31 Jan 2028 for yaw/pitch bearings and 31 Jan 2029 for main bearings. Suzlon already has 80%+ local content.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on West Asia-linked commodity and FX normalisation; management said most commodities other than steel are not passed through.
Working capital and finance cost: H1 finance cost already above INR250 crores vs INR300 crore full-year expectation; receivable days rising.
Execution: about 3.9 GW pending installation; installation lags deliveries and management expects the turnaround over about 12-18 months.
Competitive pressure from Adani and JSW; Suzlon's market share is 28-29% in orders and about 23% in deliveries.

Renom returns: acquisition cost questioned by analysts; profitability not yet demonstrated. Net cash figure (INR2,048 crores vs about INR2,300 crores cited) and encumbrance (40-50%) not clearly reconciled.
DTA recognition moved to annual (March 2027) from half-yearly, reducing visibility on PAT.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, order book and long-term targets, but candid and defensive on the margin miss, repeatedly attributing it to West Asia-linked commodity/FX volatility and one-off Suzlon 2.0 costs. Management was evasive on encumbered cash, the exact FX impact and finance cost guidance, and declined to restore the granular installation-stage disclosure.
key_quotes: Our focus remains on closing quality orders at regular intervals rather than achieving quarterly run rate.
Suzlon delivered 710 megawatts in Q2 with 40% jump quarter-on-quarter, making our ever highest second quarter India deliveries.
I have given my guidance that by FY31, I want to hit 40%.
I think capacity will not be a deciding factor. It's basically the pull from the projects.
